TelemetryStatus.description:
Per-reading status label.

Phase 3 widened this from a bare ``str`` validated against three values to a
closed enum covering the labels the repository actually uses. The old
three-value check rejected real data: presets 5 and 6 use WARNING, and the
ESA-ADB dumps use NOMINAL_CONTEXT and LABELLED_ANOMALY, so
``CrashDumpRequest.model_validate`` failed on scenarios 4, 5 and 6.

``normalize()`` accepts the aliases found in the existing data so no stored
payload has to be rewritten.
TelemetryStatus.title: TelemetryStatus

description:
CANONICAL telemetry reading — one channel at one time step.

Phase 3 made this the single representation of a telemetry sample. It is
deliberately SELF-DESCRIBING: everything a detector or a safety check needs
is on the entry, so no consumer has to reach for a parallel legacy array.

Before Phase 3 the bounds lived only on the legacy ``pre_fault_telemetry``
dicts while status and timing lived only on the window entries, which is why
Phase 2 found a scenario reporting zero anomalies when read from the window
alone. ``app/api/adapters.py`` merges both into this shape.

anomalous.description: Source-supplied anomaly flag, when the source provides one. SENTINEL's own verdict lives in the AnomalyReport, not here.
anomalous.title: Anomalous

baseline_mean.description: Observed baseline mean, when the source measured one
baseline_mean.title: Baseline Mean

baseline_std.description: Observed baseline standard deviation, when measured
baseline_std.title: Baseline Std

nominal_max.description: Upper bound of the nominal range
nominal_max.title: Nominal Max

nominal_min.description: Lower bound of the nominal range
nominal_min.title: Nominal Min

parameter.description: Telemetry channel designation, e.g. V_bat, channel_41
parameter.title: Parameter

relative_time_s.description: Parsed offset in seconds; negative is before the event
relative_time_s.title: Relative Time S

status.description: Per-reading status. Defaults to UNKNOWN, never to NOMINAL.

value.description: Numeric reading. None when unusable — see value_text.
value.title: Value

value_text.description: The raw reading when it is not a usable number, e.g. 'NaN' or 'DEGRADED'. Preserved so a NaN stays distinguishable from a missing sample; the old schema coerced both to None.
value_text.title: Value Text
